name: Imp
description: A small, mischievous worker imp, skilled at digging and crafting.

name: Goblin
description: A weak but eager creature, easily satisfied and easily frightened.

name: Orc
description: A brutish fighter, strong and aggressive but hard to please.

name: Warlock
description: A magical creature skilled in spells and research.

name: Troll
description: A large, slow creature excellent at crafting and heavy labor.

name: Skeleton
description: An undead warrior, tireless but fragile and mindless.

name: Demon Spawn
description: A powerful demonic entity with high combat prowess but demanding needs.

name: Giant Spider
description: A venomous giant spider that dwells in dark caves.

name: Cave Lizard
description: An aggressive reptilian that guards its territory.

name: Succubus
description: A seductive demon who specializes in torture and conversion.

name: Vampire
description: An ancient undead lord who drains life from enemies.

name: Hellhound
description: A fierce, two-headed demonic dog.

name: Bile Demon
description: A bloated, disgusting demon that excels at manufacturing and eating.

name: Zombie
description: A shambling corpse — slow and mindless, but tireless and hard to put down.

name: Ghost
description: A restless spirit — fast, fragile, and hard to strike, striking from beyond the veil.

name: Bat Swarm
description: A cloud of shrieking cave bats — individually harmless, together a fast, distracting nuisance.

name: Dark Elf
description: A swift, arrogant blademaster — devastating damage from poisoned blades, but quick to desert a poorly-run dungeon.

name: Lich
description: An archmage who traded their body for a soul-lantern. Research and ruin in equal measure.

name: Grave Hulk
description: Stitched from whatever the graveyard had spare. Slow, immensely durable, and hungry for corpses.

name: Balor
description: The pit's own general, wreathed in its own fire. Immense, immensely expensive, and utterly without fear.

name: Infernal Hound
description: A bound hunting beast that runs down anything entering the dungeon. Sees further than anything else in the pit.

name: Cultist
description: A lesser ritualist who staffs the circle and bleeds for it. Cheap, fervent, and useless outside a ritual room.

name: Hexbinder
description: A control caster. Hits for almost nothing and makes everything around it slower, weaker and easier to kill.

name: Ogre
description: An area-control brute. Slow to arrive and slower to swing, but heroes who take a maul to the ribs start looking for the way out.

name: Ironbound
description: Animate armour around a bound rune. Eats nothing, sleeps nowhere, wants no wage, and will never walk out on you.

name: Gnoll
description: A fast skirmisher that would rather patrol a corridor than hold one. Covers ground no other fighter can.

name: Kobold
description: A poor fighter and an excellent trap-keeper. Anything sprung within a few tiles of one hits half again as hard.

name: Stone Warden
description: A slow, patient worker that shores up the rock it stands beside. Walls it has tended cannot be tunnelled through.

name: Overseer
description: A command unit. Fights badly and works worse, but everything within a few tiles of it gets noticeably more done.

name: Archivist
description: Turns hours in a library into research nobody else could match. Useless in a fight and entirely aware of it.

name: Hobgoblin
description: What a goblin becomes with enough drilling. Armoured, disciplined, and no longer expendable.

name: Beastling
description: An unfinished thing that grows into whatever it is raised beside. Kennels make hounds of them; fighting pits make something worse.

name: Flesh Amalgam
description: Stitched together from whatever was to hand. No two are alike — each one is grafted with traits it did not ask for, and knows it.

name: Void-Touched
description: An amalgam that spent too long beside a ritual circle. Far stronger than what it was, and the surface world can feel it from above.

name: Shadow Stalker
description: Fights best where nothing can see it. Its base attack is modest on purpose - in an unlit corridor it is nearly double.
